title: Supported languages

Ix extracts code definitions and relationships, configuration entries, and document structure.
The entities available depend on the language or format.

<!-- supported-languages:start -->
<!-- Generated by ix-cli/scripts/sync-language-docs.mjs; do not edit. -->
Supported languages and formats (**35**):

| | | | |
|---|---|---|---|
| JavaScript | TypeScript | Python | Java |
| C | C++ | C# | Go |
| Ruby | Rust | PHP | Kotlin |
| Swift | Scala | YAML | Dockerfile |
| SQL | JSON | TOML | Markdown |
| R | SAS | Elixir | Makefile |
| Lua | Bash | PowerShell | Haskell |
| Zig | HTML | XML | HCL / Terraform |
| CSS | LaTeX | Protocol Buffers |  |
<!-- supported-languages:end -->

Some tree-sitter grammars are optional dependencies. If a grammar cannot load on your platform,
its files are not parsed. The config and data formats below use built-in text parsers.

## Special cases

- **CUDA** (`.cu`, `.cuh`) is parsed with the C++ grammar, including kernel-launch syntax
  (`kernel<<<grid, block>>>(args)`), so host-to-kernel calls appear in the graph.
- **Python stubs** (`.pyi`) are parsed as Python.

## Config and data formats

These formats yield named entities as well as file nodes and content chunks:

| Format | Extracted entities |
|---|---|
| YAML | Mapping keys as `config_entry` entities, with containment for nested mappings. |
| JSON | Object keys as `config_entry` entities, including keys in nested objects and array items. |
| TOML | Table names, dotted table prefixes, and assignment keys as `config_entry` entities. |
| SQL | Tables (`table`), views (`view`), indexes (`config_entry`), and functions, procedures and triggers (`function`) from supported `CREATE` statements. |
| Protocol Buffers | Packages (`module`), messages and enums (`class`), services (`interface`), and RPCs (`method`). |
| Dockerfile | Build stages (`config`), base images (`module`), and instructions (`config_entry`). |
| Markdown | Headings (`heading`) and YAML frontmatter (`frontmatter`), with section chunks covering heading contents. |
| LaTeX | Sections (`section`), macro definitions (`function`), environment definitions (`class`), and labels (`label`). |

For example, a Markdown heading, SQL table name or proto message name can be a target for
`ix locate` or `ix read` after ingestion. These text parsers extract supported constructs;
they do not implement every dialect or a full compiler for each format.

## Adding a language
